zones.label: Good source
zones.summary: Five formats that are open and good sources for editing.
facts: Markdown (.md) and plain text (.txt): open, plain text.
OpenDocument text (.odt): open, an international standard.
CSV (.csv): open plain text table, good for data.
SVG (.svg): open web standard for drawings, good for diagrams.

zones.label: Usually acceptable
zones.summary: The Word document is a published standard, but fidelity depends on software.
facts: Full fidelity depends on particular software.
A reasonable source format when your colleagues have a word processor.

zones.label: Poor source
zones.summary: A PDF is open but built for reading; a design-program file is closed.
facts: PDF (.pdf): an open international standard, poor as a source because it is built for reading.
A page layout or design-program file: closed, poor unless you own the program.
A PDF records how each page looks, not the structure, so changing a sentence means copying text out of the page.

quiz.question: Which zone holds the PDF, a format that is open but a poor source?
quiz.explanation: A PDF is built for reading.

quiz.question: Which zone holds the Word document?
quiz.explanation: Full fidelity depends on particular software.

quiz.question: Which zone holds Markdown, HTML, OpenDocument text, CSV, and SVG?
quiz.explanation: All five are open and good sources.

quiz.question: Which zone holds a page layout file that you can edit only if you own the program?
quiz.explanation: It is closed, so it is a poor source.
